tasks.spec:
You are implementing a rebuilt text-message appointment-recall pathway for an optometry practice. Your current working directory IS a disposable git worktree of the source repository. Edit files here directly.

BOUNDARY, read this before anything else.
- You own exactly three files and may create or modify NOTHING else: scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py, scripts/validate_v21.py, tests/test_v21_scenarios.py. You may also write generated output under build/.
- NEVER run git commit, git push, or any git write command. Leave your changes uncommitted; the harness exports them.
- NEVER call a network endpoint or external API. Everything you need is on disk.
- NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory or knowledge base.
- Do not modify any existing file in the repository. The v20 sources are reference material, not editing targets.

WHAT THIS IS. A Bland SMS pathway sends appointment-recall texts. A sender program resolves a patient by ID and starts a conversation, passing recall_patient_id and recall_cell in request_data. The pathway runs silent webhook nodes against a booking gateway, offers openings, and books one through a governed /sign route. Version 20 is live and has fourteen confirmed defects. You are generating version 21.

THE BINDING CONTRACT is contract/decisions.json in this worktree. It was authored by the senior decision-maker on this workflow and it is not yours to reinterpret. Read it first, in full. It fixes: which defects are in scope, the global-node contract with autoReturn values, the exact patient-facing opener template, what the model may and may not do with dates, the booking safety invariants, the outcome analysis schema, and the start-node guard. contract/verified-defects.md explains what each defect id means.

REFERENCE MATERIAL ALREADY IN THIS WORKTREE:
- scripts/build_v20_patient_id.py — the version 20 generator. Model your generator on it and REUSE its helper functions rather than rewriting them: webhook(), waiting(), message(), end(), edge(), sanitize_graph(), normalized(), request_json(), bland_key(). Import it or copy the helper shapes; do not invent a different node schema.
- scripts/validate_v20.py — the version 20 structural validator. Extend its approach.
- tests/test_v20_scenarios.py — the existing scenario suite. Follow its style.
- graph/v20_sanitized.json — the current live graph, for reference on node and edge shape.
- docs/mott-eyecloud-endpoint-field-catalog.csv — the booking gateway contract. Which endpoints are ready, blocked, or missing. Do not invent endpoints or fields.
- docs/mott-aws-response-data-inventory.md — approved response mappings per endpoint.
- tasks/v20-patient-id-two-slot-product-contract.md — the safety contract version 20 was built against. It still holds.

DELIVERABLE 1: scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py
A deterministic generator that accepts --out PATH and writes the version 21 graph as JSON. Running it twice with different output paths must produce byte-identical files. It must NOT call any network endpoint; generation is purely local. Do not add a mint or upload path; provider writes are not yours.

The graph it produces must contain exactly these nineteen nodes, using exactly these ids:
  Webhooks (silent, skipUserResponse true): n_identity (the start node), n_availability, n_conflict_1, n_conflict_2, n_sign_1, n_sign_2
  Patient-facing: n_opener, n_mixed_clarify, n_negotiate, n_confirmation, n_office
  End nodes: e_safe_identity, e_safe_failure, e_booking_failed, e_booked, e_stop, e_not_me, e_existing, e_timeout

Node-by-node requirements:
- n_identity is the only start node (isStart true). It posts /patient-search with the patient id and the phone the sender already resolved, revalidating that the pair binds to exactly one patient. Version 20's separate n_contact_lookup node is DELETED because the sender already made that identical call; do not recreate it. n_identity must carry an explicit guard that routes to e_safe_identity when recall_patient_id is empty or still an unresolved template string, evaluated before any other routing.
- n_availability posts /availability for first availability and extracts slot_count plus the slot 1 and slot 2 start, end, and doctor values. It routes on slot_count with SEPARATE deterministic edges for exactly one opening and for two or more, so suppressing the second slot is decided by an edge and not left to the model.
- n_opener is the first patient-visible message. Its prompt must interpolate patient_first and all four of slot_1_start, slot_1_end, slot_2_start, slot_2_end, and must instruct rendering in America/New_York. Use the opener template from contract/decisions.json verbatim as the message text.
- n_mixed_clarify must also interpolate slot_1_start and slot_1_end and name the America/New_York display rule. Version 20 named no times here at all, which is the same defect as the opener.
- n_negotiate is the availability negotiation loop and the ONLY node that owns the availability tool. It is a global node. Its extracted variables must include conflict, book_error and time_pref_relaxed alongside the slot and preference variables, so stale booking-conflict state is cleared on every new search. Its prompt must NOT instruct the model to normalize or compute calendar dates; the patient's own date phrase passes through to the gateway, which owns a deterministic resolver.
- n_office is a global node carrying the office-direction sentence. Define that sentence ONCE as a module constant and reference it; version 20 had three copies.
- n_conflict_1 and n_conflict_2 post /conflict-check for their matching slot. n_sign_1 and n_sign_2 post /sign. Keep this mirrored spine; do not collapse it into a single chosen-slot pair. The exact start, end and doctor values the gateway returned are what get sent.
- n_confirmation is reachable only on book_success true.

Global nodes: set isGlobal true, a non-empty globalLabel describing the trigger, and enableGlobalAutoReturn exactly as contract/decisions.json declares for that node. The six globals are n_negotiate, n_office, e_stop, e_not_me, e_existing and e_timeout. Because they are global, do NOT hand-wire per-node STOP, NOT ME, existing-appointment or timeout edges the way version 20 did; that duplication is defect F6 and removing it is the point.

IMPORTANT DESIGN RISK you must handle: n_negotiate and e_existing can both plausibly match a reply like "can we move it to Thursday". Write their globalLabel text so the triggers do not collide: the negotiation loop owns wanting a different time for THIS new appointment, and the existing-appointment exit owns a DIFFERENT appointment the patient already has. Make that distinction explicit in both labels.

Every webhook node must set Authorization to exactly the string {{ SECRET.MottGatewayToken }} and retryAttempts to 0. Never write a literal credential. Booking uses /sign only with verb appt.book and reason new-booking and no allow_conflict field. The legacy /book, /reschedule and /cancel routes are edge-denied and must not appear. Every edge must carry a non-empty label. The graph must also carry an analysis_options object holding the outcome schema fields named in contract/decisions.json.

Size targets: at most 24 nodes and at most 46 edges. Version 20 was 21 nodes and 56 edges; the globals are what buy the reduction.

DELIVERABLE 2: scripts/validate_v21.py
A structural validator that loads the generated graph and exits non-zero with a printed reason for each violation. It must check at minimum: exactly one start node and that it is n_identity; no orphaned nodes; no unlabeled edges; no literal credential anywhere; every webhook Authorization equals the secret reference; every webhook retryAttempts is 0; the opener prompt references all four slot variables; no prompt instructs date normalization; n_negotiate clears conflict and book_error; each conflict node precedes its matching sign node; confirmation is gated on book_success true. Print WHY each check failed, not just that it failed. Accept an optional --graph PATH and default to build/v21_a.json.

DELIVERABLE 3: tests/test_v21_scenarios.py
A pytest suite in the style of tests/test_v20_scenarios.py, covering at minimum: the opener renders two slots when two exist and exactly one when one exists; a relative date phrase reaches the gateway unmodified; conflict and book_error are cleared on a second negotiation round so no repeat apology occurs; the negotiation loop is reachable from the confirmation node; the office node is reachable from the mixed-clarify node; an empty recall_patient_id refuses at the start node before any gateway call; a taken slot routes back to negotiation rather than to confirmation; an ordinary booking failure ends without claiming success.

HOW TO VERIFY YOUR OWN WORK, from the worktree root:
  mkdir -p build
  python3 scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py --out build/v21_a.json
  python3 scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py --out build/v21_b.json
  diff build/v21_a.json build/v21_b.json
  python3 scripts/validate_v21.py
  python3 -m pytest tests/test_v21_scenarios.py -q

All five must succeed before you finish. An independent validator owned by the orchestrator will also run against your generated graph; it enforces the contract above, so satisfying only your own validator is not enough.

HARD RULES. Do not invent gateway endpoints, request fields or response paths; the catalog is authoritative. Do not weaken a booking safety invariant to make the graph simpler. Do not write a validator or a test that cannot fail. Do not commit. Do not touch any file outside your three owned paths and build/.
tasks.verified: the generator is deterministic, its graph passes an orchestrator-owned gate derived from the Fable decision packet, the worker's own validator and the scenario suite both pass, the worker stayed inside its three owned paths, and the patch plus generated graph were exported out of the worktree before deletion
